Thought: I need to determine which compound, when reacted with sodium cyanide (NaCN) in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), would produce a nitrile. 

Nitriles have the general formula R-C≡N. They are typically formed through nucleophilic substitution reactions where the cyanide ion (CN⁻) acts as a nucleophile and displaces a good leaving group like a halide.

Let me analyze each option:

A. 1-Bromo-3-methylbutane: This is a primary alkyl halide. The bromine (Br) is a good leaving group, and the cyanide ion can perform an SN2 reaction, displacing the bromine to form a nitrile.

B. 2-Methylbutane: This is an alkane with no reactive functional groups. It has no good leaving groups for the cyanide to displace.

C. 3-Methyl-1-butanol: This is an alcohol. While alcohols can be converted to better leaving groups (like tosylates or mesylates), they don't directly react with cyanide to form nitriles.

D. 3-Methyl-1-butene: This is an alkene. Cyanide typically doesn't add directly to alkenes under these conditions.

Based on this analysis, 1-Bromo-3-methylbutane (option A) is the only compound that would readily react with sodium cyanide to produce a nitrile through an SN2 reaction.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
